full_judgment:
10. Learned Advocate Mr Mahbubur Rahman appearing for the condemned prisoner Siraj Mondal and learned Advocate Mr Showkat Ali Khan appearing for the accused appellant Matiar Rahman alias Montu have seriously assailed the impugned judgment and order of conviction and sentence passed by the learned Additional Sessions Judge in that the learned Judge did not take into consideration the fact of departure from and embellishment of the first information report which was the earliest recorded version of the prosecution case, during the course of trial. The learned Judge, they have argued, convicted the condemned prisoner and the accused appellant in breach of legal norms and recognised mode of assessment and appreciation of evidence having not taken into consideration that the evidence of two eye-witnesses namely, PW 5 Abdul Mannan and PW 12 Abdullah were full of contradictions making the prosecution case unreliable. It has been argued by them that the learned Judge did not also take into consideration that the GD entry which was the first in point of time relating to information of the occurrence was the real first information report which was suppressed while the information which was treated as first information report in the instant case was, in fact, a statement under section 161 of the Criminal Procedure Code and was not admissible in evidence as such. According to them, learned Judge did not take into consideration that the occurrence having admittedly taken place in the darkness of night it was unusual on the part of the witnesses to recognise the accused in focus of the electric torches held by them (accused) for accomplishing their own criminal acts and that they should ever direct the focus to themselves for their own identification to the witnesses at their own peril. They have further argued that prosecution examined a handful of 14 witnesses leaving 15 other charge-sheet cited witnesses un-examined which gave rise to a presumption in favour of the condemned prisoner and the accused appalled under section 114(g) of the Evidence Act for withholding such witnesses. In support of their submissions they cited different case laws which we propose to deal with at the relevant places. 

 35. Let us now consider the status of the four star witnesses of the prosecution in relation to the deceased. We have found that the deceased was a candidate for parliamentary election as a nominee from JSD (Rob). He was president of the District Committee and a member of the central committee of the party. PW 1 Shukur Ali was his full brother and was an activist of his political party. PW 5 Abdul Mannan was also an activist of the deceased. He was appointed contractor during the Upazila chairmanship of the deceased. This witness admitted that accused Afu (Israil) was elected Upazila Chairman by defeating the deceased (in 1990). PW 10 Bashiruddin Kachi admitted that he was the Joint Secretary of Mirpur Upazila JSD and also used to work as a contractor during the Upazila Chairmanship of the deceased. He was defeated in Malihat UP election by the accused Ismail. Both he and the deceased were in custody together in connection with murder cases. PW 12 Abdullah was a contractor. He was secretary of Mirpur Thana JSD. He joined active politics and became associated with the deceased since parliamentary election in 1979. All the said four witnesses were thus close activists of the deceased while the accused belonged to the rival group. They were, therefore, interested and partisan witnesses. No independent witness, even not a hearsay one, came to support the prosecution case corroborating the said 4 witnesses involving the accused. Over and above, out of as many as 29 CS cited witnesses prosecution examined only 14 witnesses leaving majority of them unexamined without any plausible explanation which thus introduced a presumption in favour of the defence under section 114(g) of the Evidence Act that they would not have supported the case of the prosecution in case of their examination or production before the court.
